response.sql: WITH u AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(CAST(product_quantity AS INTEGER)) AS units FROM Order_Items WHERE product_quantity IS NOT NULL GROUP BY product_id), s AS (SELECT product_id, units, units * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(units) FROM u) AS share FROM u), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.units) AS combined_units, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS average_excess_over_overall_average FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Order items with a NULL product_quantity are dropped before grouping. A product whose items all have NULL quantity therefore does not appear and does not count in the average over products.
Shares are computed as decimals (units * 1.0 / total), so there is no integer division.
product_quantity strings are numeric and are cast directly to integer.

alternatives.interpretation: Products whose quantities are all missing stay in the product list with 0 units. They count in the average over products and pull the average share down.
alternatives.sql: WITH u AS (SELECT product_id, COALESCE(SUM(CAST(product_quantity AS INTEGER)), 0) AS units FROM Order_Items GROUP BY product_id), s AS (SELECT product_id, units, units * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(units) FROM u) AS share FROM u), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.units) AS combined_units, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS average_excess_over_overall_average FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share
